ingredientGroups.heading: The leaves (the wrap chassis — a generous double-handful of leaves per person)

ingredients.item: green leaf lettuce — the everyday wrap, mild cup
red leaf or butter lettuce — the tender alternative
perilla leaves — the flavor wrap, anise-mint
bunch napa cabbage leaves, the tender inner ones , optional — the crisp snap wrap

ingredientGroups.heading: The herbs and crunch (threaded into the wraps)

ingredients.item: Garlic cloves, sliced into thick coins , raw
Thinly sliced onion, soaked 10 minutes in cold water

ingredientGroups.heading: The table's other half (beside the platter, from this site)

ingredients.item: Ssamjang , gireumjang , the scallion-soy dip , a bowl of rice, and the banchan board

instructions.heading: The platter's arrangement — bigger leaves under, herbs through
instructions.action: The platter's arrangement — bigger leaves under, herbs through. The lettuce cups fanned around the platter's rim as the chassis layer, perilla and cabbage tucked inside the ring, garlic coins, chili, and drained onion in small piles at the center where every hand reaches.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the geometry test: every diner, from any seat, can reach a cup, a perilla leaf, and a center pile without asking anyone to pass. The platter turns; build it round.

instructions.heading: The wrap build, the table's own method
instructions.action: The wrap build, the table's own method. The sequence this site's M-records keep citing: one leaf (or a lettuce cup lined with one perilla leaf — the double-bottom, the connoisseur's build), a thin swipe of ssamjang or a finger-dip of gireumjang, the meat while it is still hot, a garlic coin or chili slice or onion thread, a pinch of rice if the wrap runs meat-only, fold stem-side over, tuck the sides, one bite.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the fold closes without tearing and delivers everything in a single bite: that is the doneness of a ssam. Two bites means the leaf was overfilled; a torn wrap means the sauce ran to the fold — swipe thinner, higher.

instructions.heading: The pacing — the platter sets the meal's rhythm
instructions.action: The pacing — the platter sets the meal's rhythm. Meat, wrap, rice, banchan, repeat. The leaves are the meal's brakes and its carriers; a table that runs out of leaves starts eating meat with chopsticks alone, and the meal quietly becomes a different, heavier thing.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the end-of-meal test: empty leaf platter, empty ssamjang bowl, and the grill's last pieces going into the last wraps — the platter planned to the end is the record's real success metric.

storageNotes: Washed leaves keep 2–3 days in paper towel in a bag in the fridge — the make-ahead that makes a weeknight grill possible. Herbs, 2 days in water.

Variations: steamed cabbage leaves and blanched kale for winter's sturdy wraps; thin rice-paper wrappers at the table's edge for the fusion lane; the pickled perilla (#B24) as a wrap-within-a-wrap, the double-perilla build.
